children: China's official manufacturing gauge rebounded more than expected in August as output and market demand recovered, though activity remained in contraction for a second straight month.
The official manufacturing purchasing managers index inched higher to 49.8 in August from 49.2 in July, said the National Bureau of Statistics on Monday.

The result beat the 49.5 forecast made by economists in a Wall Street Journal survey. Nonetheless, it was still the second consecutive month below the 50 threshold, which signals a contraction in activity, while a reading above 50 indicates expansion.

The production subindex rose to 50.4 in August, compared with 49.9 in July. The subindex for total new orders increased to 50.6 from 48.5 in July, while new export orders rebounded to 50.1 from 49.6 in July.
Meanwhile, China's nonmanufacturing PMI, which covers both service and construction activity, stayed unchanged at 49.0 in August, the statistics bureau said.
The subindex tracking service activity remained unchanged at 49.3 in August, while the construction subindex fell slightly to 46.9 from 47.0.
